vts_name: Saint Petersburg VTS / regional VTS for the eastern Gulf of Finland
vts_boundary_basis: Current Rosmorport defines the Saint Petersburg VTS area in Russian territorial waters east of 026°30'E and includes established vessel routes; Sommers is an operational radar post. Current UKHO places the Sommers route/reporting point within Saint Petersburg Coastal VTS.
reporting_boundary_basis: GOFREP is defined for international waters; Fintraffic separates the Russian-maintained territorial-water TSS from the four GOFREP TSS it names.
evidence_summary: Operational VTS association confirmed; no IMO mandatory reporting-scheme association established for this Russian territorial-water TSS.
source_date: Rosmorport current page; UKHO Weekly Edition 11/2026; IMO Ships' Routeing 2025

vts_name: Saint Petersburg VTS / regional VTS for the eastern Gulf of Finland
vts_boundary_basis: Current Rosmorport VTS area begins east of 026°30'E in Russian territorial waters and includes established vessel routes; Gogland is an operational radar post. Current UKHO gives Saint Petersburg Coastal VTS Sector 1 west of 028°00'E.
reporting_boundary_basis: Fintraffic names the GOFREP TSS as Hankoniemi, Porkkala, Kalbådagrund and Kõpu, then distinguishes Russian-maintained TSS in Russian territorial waters.
evidence_summary: Operational VTS association confirmed; no IMO mandatory reporting-scheme association established for this Russian territorial-water TSS.
source_date: Rosmorport current page; UKHO Weekly Edition 11/2026; IMO Ships' Routeing 2025

vts_name: Saint Petersburg VTS / regional VTS for the eastern Gulf of Finland
vts_boundary_basis: Current Rosmorport defines the VTS area east of 026°30'E in Russian territorial waters along established vessel routes. The IMO Rodsher TSS lies immediately east of 026°30'E around Russian Rodsher Island; earlier Russian navigation rules explicitly place the Rodsher TSS in the coastal VTS area and current sources confirm the service remains operational.
reporting_boundary_basis: GOFREP is defined for international waters; current Fintraffic separates Russian territorial-water TSS from the four GOFREP TSS it names.
evidence_summary: Operational VTS association confirmed; no IMO mandatory reporting-scheme association established.
source_date: Rosmorport current page; UKHO Weekly Edition 11/2026; IMO Ships' Routeing 2025

vts_boundary_basis: No operational VTS boundary was found covering this offshore TSS; Fintraffic distinguishes Finnish/Estonian VTS areas from GOFREP.
reporting_boundary_basis: IMO MSC.231(82) draws the Central Reporting Line through the midpoint of the Kalbådagrund separation zone; the current Fintraffic GOFREP material names Kalbådagrund among the Gulf of Finland TSS.
evidence_summary: GOFREP association confirmed. Helsinki Traffic is a GOFREP reporting centre, not evidence that Helsinki VTS covers this offshore TSS.
source_date: IMO Ships' Routeing 2025; current Fintraffic GOFREP material

vts_boundary_basis: No operational VTS boundary was found covering this offshore TSS; Fintraffic distinguishes Finnish/Estonian VTS areas from GOFREP.
reporting_boundary_basis: IMO MSC.231(82) draws the Central Reporting Line through the midpoint of the Porkkala separation zone; the current Fintraffic GOFREP material names Porkkala among the Gulf of Finland TSS.
evidence_summary: GOFREP association confirmed. Helsinki Traffic and Helsinki VTS are separate operational concepts and must not be merged.
source_date: IMO Ships' Routeing 2025; current Fintraffic GOFREP material

vts_boundary_basis: Hanko VTS does not cover the IMO TSS: the TSS lies around 59°24.5'N–59°30.0'N and 022°25.0'E–022°45.0'E, while the current Hanko VTS southern boundary is at 59°40.5'N.
reporting_boundary_basis: IMO/GOFREP places the Central Reporting Line through the Hankoniemi TSS; current Fintraffic GOFREP material names Hankoniemi among the four Gulf of Finland TSS.
evidence_summary: GOFREP association confirmed. The nearby Hanko VTS boundary is geographically separate from this offshore TSS.
source_date: IMO Ships' Routeing 2025; current Fintraffic Hanko VTS and GOFREP material

vts_boundary_basis: Estonian Transport Administration distinguishes the VTS area from GOFREP and requires a report when entering Western VTS across the western reporting line starting at Kõpu. No source establishes the offshore Kõpu TSS itself as inside Western VTS.
reporting_boundary_basis: IMO/GOFREP places the Central/Western reporting geometry through the Kõpu TSS; current Estonian and Fintraffic material treats Kõpu as part of GOFREP.
evidence_summary: GOFREP association confirmed. Western VTS is a distinct Estonian VTS area and coverage of this offshore TSS is not established.
source_date: IMO Ships' Routeing 2025; Estonian Transport Administration; Fintraffic

vts_boundary_basis: Current Traficom decision places the southern edge of Bothnia VTS from Ritgrund lighthouse 63°25.5'N 021°30.5'E to the territorial-sea boundary at 63°40.0'N 021°31.0'E, then north to Tornio. The IMO Norra Kvarken TSS lies west of that boundary, at roughly 020°37'E–021°04'E. Sweden's current VTS directory lists no Kvarken VTS.
reporting_source_id: No applicable system appears in the authoritative IMO 2025 Part I mandatory reporting inventory.
source_date: Bothnia VTS requires an advance report from Finland-bound vessels before Nordvalen, but this is an approach procedure and does not place the Norra Kvarken TSS inside the VTS area.
accessed_date: IMO Ships' Routeing 2025; Traficom VTS decision; current Fintraffic and Swedish Maritime Administration material
